source.display_title: 06/06/2026 - Vishal Patel x Andrew Musial  — Lost

setter.evidence: No setter referenced and no suffix in the title. Inbound from Trevor's own content: 'I've seen his videos online. They keep popping up on feeds and stuff' and 'I've been kind of watching his Insta for a while'. The rep opens by introducing himself cold: 'my name is Andrew, and I'm a senior advisor here with Trevor's team'.

prospect.name: Vishal Patel
prospect.location: United States — commutes about an hour each way to an office; travelling to Warsaw, Puerto Rico, Washington DC and Orlando over the following six weeks
prospect.occupation: Owner of several medical companies — pharmacies plus clinic back-office support services, with around 50 staff in India. Pharmacist by training with a doctoral degree; no longer practises.
prospect.family_status: Divorced, and currently engaged — 'I'm trying to get married, but yeah, so I have a lot of expenses coming up.' No children mentioned.
prospect.training_background: Aims for the gym about three times a week in the mornings but has lost consistency to work and travel. Owns kettlebells at home but does not use them on any routine basis. Plays racquet sports, mainly pickleball. Former basketball player; has not jumped or run any significant amount in nearly ten years. Meal preps around 100g cooked rice, 100g protein and vegetables, supplemented with delivered prepared meals. Around 3,000-4,000 steps a day against a 10,000 target, tracked on an Apple Watch. Target weight 210-215 lb.
prospect.medical: Ruptured patellar tendon requiring emergency surgery, almost ten years ago — 'all I hear is a pop, and my look, and my kneecap is in my thigh.' It followed a pre-existing partial tear in the same tendon from basketball. Still symptomatic under load: bodyweight squats are fine, but 'if I go super heavy, like on a squat rack, then I notice it a little bit... it will start throbbing after a while if I put a really hard squat-intensive workout.' Separately, right elbow cracked in a fall at a concert venue, healed to roughly 90% range of motion — cannot extend fully overhead, cannot dead hang for long, and has never been able to do a pull-up. No back pain and no chronic conditions. Hereditary history was not asked; he volunteered that his grandparents stayed active into their late eighties.

signals: Motivation is holding on to function rather than gaining anything, and he states it in almost the exact terms of the archetype: 'I'm trying to make some changes, so I'm not a slave to my own body' and 'My biggest fear is to be in a body when I'm later in my life that... It's like my coffin, like my tombstone.'

Health-literate and speaks from inside the system — a pharmacist who owns pharmacies and clinic services: 'I've seen so much in the healthcare field and I'm just like, yeah, I need to make some changes for sure.'

The defining preserver economics: high nominal success, low discretionary liquidity. 'All my money is basically tied into my company that I don't really pay myself enough. You know, like, I just keep everything back in the company.' $2,000 available now against $6,000.

Frames the purchase as insurance rather than ambition: 'Again, I'm trying to take some preventative measures, mainly.' When offered a magic wand he could not name a win — 'I never really thought about that.'

CAVEAT ON THE ASSIGNMENT, which is why confidence is 0.6: he is 41, not older, and is not under active medical management. He also wants to lose 40 lb, which is a gain rather than a hold. The archetype is assigned on psychology and liquidity, not on age. the_rebuilder was the alternative — he has lost a former self, having not jumped or run in a decade — but he explicitly declines to chase it back: 'Those extreme sports days are behind me... I don't really have any desire, to be honest with you.'

goals.text: Lose about 40 lb, from 250 down to 210-215, and stop bulking up every time he trains
Age gracefully and stay independent rather than end up dependent on someone to move him around
Take load off the knees before it becomes a problem — 'I know I'm going to have issues later in my life, but I don't want to carry this weight'
Train efficiently at home and while travelling instead of losing hours to a packed gym
Find something he actually enjoys enough to stick with — 'I'll give it a fair shake, and if it's something that I enjoy, then I'll totally be able to stick with it'
Possibly jump again, and play some basketball — he has not jumped since the knee rupture almost ten years ago

pains.text: Surgically repaired ruptured patellar tendon that still throbs under heavy squat-intensive loading
Right elbow limited to about 90% range of motion — cannot dead hang for long and has never done a pull-up
Fear of being trapped in a failing body of his own making — 'you have a body that's failing you, and you could have made some changes in your life to make that not the case'
An hour's commute each way and back-to-back meetings leave only an unappealing early-morning window
His local gym is wall-to-wall packed from 3pm to 10pm and he loses hours waiting on machines behind people filming
Monthly conference travel destroys any routine — four trips including Europe and Puerto Rico in roughly six weeks
Sedentary at 3,000-4,000 steps a day, desk-bound going from meeting to meeting
Sweet tooth he knows he should limit — 'I do like to indulge myself in things like that, which I know I should be limiting, but eh, it is what it is'
Came out of a divorce into an area where he had few friends, which is why he joined the kickball league where the knee ruptured

objections.raw_quote: I hope so. I don't know what else will... I mean, again, it's something that I would have to, I've never done a program like this, so I can't really give you a solid yes or no.
objections.rep_response: PROPOSED LABEL: 'low_conviction_commitment'. The rep correctly refused the hedge and used a legitimate takeaway — 'Trevor is like, he's gonna be on you. So if you already feel that I will probably fall off after the first month, it doesn't make sense to actually go for it then.' The prospect then disclosed that his agreement is unreliable by temperament: 'this is just my personality. I'm pretty timid. So I don't really know what to say half the time. So I just kind of throw in words.' The rep pushed on to a yes anyway, including 'Is that loud enough?' and 'it has to be, yeah, coming from your guts', and treated the resulting 'Yes' as the commitment gate.

objections.raw_quote: I wasn't expecting this to be this high. I have to think about it, to be honest with you. Can we do a monthly installment, or is it 6k all at once?
objections.rep_response: Deflected the instalment question rather than answering it — 'Do you ask for any reason? Because most of the guys just take it up front' — then reframed to 'is it the money thing or something else that's coming up for you?' The prospect made the expectation gap explicit a minute later: 'I was thinking maybe around $3,000 or $4,000, but $6,000 is pretty, $1,000 a month, basically.'

objections.raw_quote: Again, this is, this is going to be a little bit more of a tougher decision for me, to be honest with you. I might have to take some time to think about it.
objections.rep_response: Ran the money play thoroughly and then failed to use what it produced. He isolated, asked permission for an honest financial conversation, and took the most complete financial picture in this batch — $2,000 cash on hand, roughly $3,000 left over monthly, credit cards with high available credit that he will not carry balances on, and no investments because capital is tied up in his company. Having established that $2,000 down plus two months of surplus covers $6,000, he proposed no plan at all and instead offered a smaller product at $4,000.

objections.raw_quote: Well, I mean, I'm trying to get married, but yeah, so I have a lot of expenses coming up. So I'm trying to earmark things out. I don't think I have the extra expenditure right now for spending 6k.
objections.rep_response: Answered with a single aesthetic reframe — 'Wouldn't it be like a crazy idea to, when you're getting married, to actually look lean and mean?' — which the prospect conceded in principle and rejected in practice: 'Yeah, for sure, but I have a lot of expenses.' None of the scripted not-the-right-time moves ran, despite the prospect having said minutes earlier that his schedule will not ease 'in the next 10 years'.

objections.raw_quote: I don't know. I have to think about it, my friend.
objections.rep_response: Pushed back on the prospect ending the call — 'Do you really think I will give up on you that easily?', then 'Oh, you want to hang up on me already?' and 'Oh, man. Don't do that. Like, come on.' He then ran the zoom-out and offered the three-month tier, and asked the correct diagnostic question twice: 'what's coming up actually for you that's preventing you from getting started?' That produced the final answer and the end of the call.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Offered in principle and never built. 'Most of the guys take care of the investment upfront. But for certain clients, I don't feel that's the best thing. Based on their situation, so we break it up... So we don't have set payment plans. It's all customized depending on what's best for the particular client.' No schedule, deposit or instalment figure was ever proposed, including after the prospect disclosed $2,000 available immediately and about $3,000 of monthly surplus. The only structure offered was a smaller three-month product at $4,000 with a stated $2,000 top-up to reach six months.

prospect_financials.disclosed: Cash he could put down today: $2,000. Left over monthly after bills and groceries: around $3,000. Holds credit cards with high available credit but declines to carry balances — 'I don't like carrying balances for credit... It's just going to cause more issues later.' No meaningful investments: 'all my money is basically tied into my company that I don't really pay myself enough.' Significant upcoming wedding expenses. Anchored expectation for the programme was $3,000-$4,000.

evidence: Explicit decline at the end, with no next step and no future contact agreed: 'Financially, I'm just not in a stable position to make this. So I guess I'll have to go back to what I've been trying to do and figure it out. Yeah, I'm going to have to figure it out on my own, but again, thank you so much for talking to me.'
Both the $6,000 and the improvised $4,000 tier were refused. On the three-month option: 'that's just, yeah, I had to think about it. Like, that's just too much for me. I'm sorry.'
No payment, no link, no follow-up call booked, no contact details exchanged. The rep closed with 'All right, man. No worries.'

COUNTER-EVIDENCE toward follow_up: earlier at 00:39:50 he framed it as a pause rather than a no — 'I guess for now we can table this conversation and I can take a look more deep at my finances and figure out what I want to do' — and the commercial interest was genuine throughout. It is scored lost because his final position, three minutes later, was that he would solve it alone.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE on the cause: he was never fully committed to begin with. He declined to give a yes at the commitment check and disclosed that his verbal agreement is unreliable, so the price objection landed on a foundation that had not been built.

notable.note: The most script-faithful money play in this batch produced the only outright loss in it, and the reason is what the rep did with the answers rather than the questions he asked. He ran eight of the ten Objection C moves and obtained a complete financial picture — $2,000 available now, about $3,000 of monthly surplus, credit available but unwanted, capital locked in the business. That picture shows $6,000 is reachable across roughly two months. He then structured nothing and offered a smaller product at $4,000 instead, which the prospect also refused. Two other things a principal should see. The prospect disclosed a surgically repaired ruptured patellar tendon that still throbs under load and an elbow that will not fully extend overhead, at 250 lb, and was moved toward loaded kettlebell training with no clinician clearance sought. And the commitment gate failed openly: he said 'I can't really give you a solid yes or no' and then 'I'm pretty timid... I just kind of throw in words', and the rep proceeded to price on a yes he had just been told not to trust.

quality.notes: Video was off for the prospect throughout, which appears to have worsened attribution. Inversions are frequent on both short and long turns: 'Like the commute to work takes you a lot of time?' at 00:04:15 is the rep under Vishal's label; 'From 3 p.m. to 10 p.m., it's packed' at 00:04:43 is the prospect under the rep's label; 'Tell me more about what happened' at 00:06:57 is the rep inside a Vishal-labelled block, and the whole knee-injury narrative that follows is split across both labels; 'It's like around, I think on average, like 3,000 to 4,000 steps a day' at 00:06:11 is the prospect under the rep's label; 'Especially I've seen so much in the healthcare field' at 00:16:30 is the prospect under the rep's label. The 00:39:24 to 00:40:27 stretch covering the takeaway and the attempt to end the call is almost entirely inverted. Roles resolved from content. Timestamps reliable. Several short passages are garbled beyond recovery, including the cash-on-hand figure which reads 'Like,,000?' and is recoverable only from the rep's confirmation immediately after, '2K. Okay.'
